decision_points.question: Which covariates make up the primary adjusted model's adjustment set?
decision_points.why_rival: each names a different set of covariates the primary model adjusts for (games+position, games only, log-games only); an analyst fits one such specification as the main model

decision_points.question: How is the effect's sensitivity to covariate selection tested by removing or varying covariates in the adjustment set?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a different way of stripping down the adjustment set for a robustness refit (drop all, drop yellowCards, drop referee-bias terms, drop an unspecified covariate, sweep a nested ladder); none of these co-occur, consistent with being rival forms of the same drop-covariate check

decision_points.question: Is the adjustment set expanded by adding covariates as a robustness check?
decision_points.why_rival: adding a covariate is its own robustness slot, kept separate from the drop-covariate slot because it co-occurs with option 18 (an analyst adds one covariate and drops another in the same run)

decision_points.question: What regression family is used to estimate the effect — logistic or linear probability model?
decision_points.why_rival: the analyst picks one functional form for the regression; logistic and the (duplicate) linear-probability specifications are mutually exclusive answers to how the binary outcome is modeled

decision_points.question: How is the crude, unadjusted association assessed?
decision_points.why_rival: each is an alternative bare-bones test of the skin-tone/red-card association with no covariate adjustment (chi-square, two-proportion z, Spearman, unadjusted logistic OR, raw-difference-plus-bivariate); an analyst chooses one crude test, and none co-occur with each other

decision_points.question: Is skin tone modeled on its original continuous scale rather than categorized?
decision_points.why_rival: treating skin tone as continuous is one rival coding of the exposure, incompatible with dichotomizing or banding it

decision_points.question: Are all skin-tone categories retained, or is the sample collapsed to extreme groups?
decision_points.why_rival: keeping all bands / all levels versus dropping the middle to compare extreme groups are opposing dispositions of the skin-tone categories; an analyst does one

decision_points.question: Where is the skin-tone dichotomization cutoff set?
decision_points.why_rival: each picks a different threshold (or sweep of thresholds) at which the skin-tone scale is split into dark/light; they are rival cutoff choices for the same dichotomy

decision_points.question: Is skin tone measured at the individual player level or as a club average?
decision_points.why_rival: the level at which the exposure is aggregated is its own choice, distinct from how the scale is coded

decision_points.question: Is a skin-tone by referee-bias moderation interaction tested, and how?
decision_points.why_rival: these settle whether/how the moderation is evaluated (fit the interaction, LR-test it vs main effects, joint LR-test the interaction terms) — rival ways of answering the same moderation question

decision_points.question: How are the standard errors computed?
decision_points.why_rival: the choice of HC3 robust standard errors is a single slot for how uncertainty is estimated

decision_points.question: How is the significance of the skin-tone coefficient formally tested?
decision_points.why_rival: the two-sided Wald z-test is one choice of inference procedure for the model coefficient

decision_points.question: What regression diagnostics are computed?
decision_points.why_rival: requesting fit/collinearity/R2 statistics versus a Durbin-Watson autocorrelation test are alternative diagnostic checks reported for the model

decision_points.question: Are goalkeepers included in the analytic sample?
decision_points.why_rival: whether goalkeepers are in or out defines who the study is about — a single inclusion decision

decision_points.question: Which prepared analytic subset of the data is used?
decision_points.why_rival: selecting the d4.test analytic subset settles which processed dataset the analysis runs on

decision_points.question: Is the analysis stratified into subgroups (e.g., by league), and how?
decision_points.why_rival: re-running the model separately per league versus computing unadjusted risk differences within subgroups are rival ways to stratify rather than pool the data

decision_points.question: How are raw group red-card rates reported descriptively?
decision_points.why_rival: reporting raw unadjusted rates by group with no formal test is a distinct descriptive-presentation slot

decision_points.question: What covariate-balance descriptives are reported?
decision_points.why_rival: a Table 1 of covariate means by group is its own descriptive step, done alongside (co-occurring with) the outcome reporting

decision_points.question: How are the primary and sensitivity specifications summarized together?
decision_points.why_rival: assembling a side-by-side comparison table is a single choice about how results are collated for presentation

decision_points.question: What confidence level is adopted for interval estimates?
decision_points.why_rival: fixing the 95% confidence level is one slot for the width of reported intervals

decision_points.question: What overall verdict on the hypothesis is declared?
decision_points.why_rival: declaring the hypothesis SUPPORTED is the concluding call the analysis must make
